In that exact capture the values are NOT identical: the row "European Monthly Weather HDD Futures & Options" reads Electronic Trading (Sunday) = 17:00-15:00 while all 20 other rows read 17:00-15:15. The same 17:00-15:00 anomaly is present on the 2009-07-27 weather-hours capture and on the platform-wide 2012-05-28 and 2012-06-07 trading_hours captures. But the claim as written is refuted by the cited document, and the file should say "identical apart from a persistent typo in one European HDD cell, contradicted by that product's own spec page".

MISDESCRIBED NOTICE, and a missed effective date. The file writes that the Globex Notices of 2023-05-15 and 2023-07-31/2023-08-21 list new weather futures/options "effective Sunday 2023-05-21 (trade date 2023-05-22) and Sunday 2023-08-27 (trade date 2023-08-28)". Verbatim from https://www.cmegroup.com/notices/electronic-trading/2023/07/20230731.html: item "Listing New HDD Weather Options - August 13 ... Effective Sunday, August 13 (trade date Monday, August 14), pending completion of all regulatory review periods, the following Weather options will be listed for trading on CME Globex and for submission for clearing via CME ClearPort" (security group W7, market data channel 317); and separately item "Listing New CDD Weather Options - August 27 ... Effective Sunday, August 27 (trade date Monday, August 28) ...". Also: the 2023-05-15 item is headed "Listing New Weather Futures" and covers FUTURES only (security group HW, channel 316) — the file's phrasing "NEW weather futures/options ... effective Sunday 2023-05-21" implies options were in that May listing; they were not. These are new-city product launches, so the file's conclusion that they are not dispositive of the legacy options' venue migration still holds.

EVIDENTIAL GAP OVERSTATED — see unsourced item 2. "After 2022-06-30 CME's product pages became fully client-rendered, so no archived capture resolves the interval" is false; eleven-plus server-rendered captures resolve it, running through 2025-02-18.

The file's load-bearing sentence for keeping the equity and crypto SQF roots together is: "There is no document in which the equity SQF grid and the crypto SQF grid differ." result.strongest_counterargument:
The strongest case against several profiles is that the six T values may be contract EXPIRIES misread as session closes — and the crate would then be inventing six grids out of one.

Nothing in any retrieved document states a Monday-Thursday session close at T. What SER-8968R states verbatim is (a) a weekly range, "ECES; ECNQ; ERTY; ECYM: Sunday 5:00 p.m.- Friday 3:00 p.m.", (b) a queue, "All Contracts: CME Globex Pre Open: Sunday 4:00 - 5:00 p.m. Monday - Thursday 4:45 - 5:00 p.m.", and (c) a relist, "Next day's Event Contract will list at 5:00 p.m." The daily dark window from T to 16:45 — which is the whole of the six-way split — is derived from those three, never quoted. And the separate "Termination of Trading" row in the same Exhibit says "Daily products: trading will terminate at the end of the daily settlement period of the Underlying Futures contract", while rulebook 2302.E, which I retrieved, scopes termination to the individual contract: "Trading shall terminate at the end of the daily settlement period for the Underlying Futures, on the Expiration Date that the Event Contract was listed for." On that reading T is when a contract dies, not when a market closes; the root's Globex envelope could be the ordinary 17:00-16:00, and one key would cover all ten.

My own retrieval sharpens this into a live contradiction the research file does not address. In CME's current specification PDF, ECES and ECNQ each list "1 event contract expiring on the last business day of Mar, Jun, or Sep" and "1 event contract expiring on the last business day of the calendar year" alongside the 0DTE contract. Under the file's model, CME halts a contract with up to a year of life left for one hour and forty-five minutes every weekday afternoon, for months, and CME never republished the hours row when it added those contracts. Under the expiry reading there is no puzzle at all. The file's product characterisation ("daily-expiring") and its quoted rationale for the six T values are both the superseded 2022 text.

Two things stop this from winning, and they are the reason I still land where I do. First, CME publishes T inside a cell headed "CME Globex Trading Hours" while giving termination its own separate row in the same Exhibit — it is not conflating them. Second, and decisively for one root, the 2026 impact assessment states the halt as an operational fact rather than an expiry: "Monday through Friday | Daily Maintenance Window (with Trade Date roll) | Close: 3:00:00 p.m. to 4:01:00 p.m. CT". For ECBTC, 15:00 is demonstrably a market close. The structural parallel to the other ten is exact but is a parallel, not a source — and ECBTC is precisely the root that has no quarter-end or year-end contract to complicate it. So the six-way split is a strong, well-motivated reading that survives; it is not a quoted fact, and the file should say so.

A weaker second counterargument, worth recording because it is the one the task asks for: there IS a contract in the group whose hours differ. ECS10/ECS11/ECS13/ECS15 are event contracts on the same E-mini S&P 500 futures, on the same exchange, in the same "Events on Futures" section of the same CME specification, and their published grid ("Sunday 6:00 p.m. - Friday 5:00 p.m. ET with a daily maintenance period from 5:00 p.m. - 6:00 p.m. ET" per SER-9624, quoted in the file's own scope warning) is materially different from ECES's. The file excludes them, correctly — but its stated reason is the grid, which is circular for family identity. The defensible line is the rulebook chapter, 23 versus 23A, and the file cannot draw that line because its chapter attributions are wrong.
